newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Bass says France, Germany better.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Bass says France, Germany better.

text.p: Sir Ian Prosser, chairman of British pub-to-hotel group Bass Plc, said on Wednesday conditions in Germany and France had reached their low point and were now on their way back up.

"Germany and France have probably bottomed out and are now on the way back up and in America we are continuing to see good economic growth. We are seeing most central banks taking action against inflation," said Prosser in an interview.

Bass hopes the new incoming Labour government will reach a decision on the group's proposed acquisition of brewer Carlsberg-Tetley in the middle of next month. "I would guess mid-June we might hear," said Prosser.

When asked what other uncertainties a change of government brought for the group, Prosser replied, "Their attitude over a minimum wage and where they would set that. I think it should be set at a relatively low figure and phased in over a period of time to give companies a chance to accommodate it."

Britain's largest trade union, UNISON, representing 1.3 million public sector workers, is asking the Labour government to impose a minimum wage of half the median male salary or 4.42 stg an hour. The Labour Party plans to set up a Low Pay Commission to take evidence from employers and unions before recommending a minimum wage.
The introduction of a minimum wage is likely to affect the food, drink and retail sector especially given the high number of part time, low-paid staff employed.

Peter Jarvis, chief executive of Whitbread Plc until June 2 when he is tipped to head up the Low Pay unit, has called for a minimum wage to be applied on a regional basis and to take account of incentive schemes offered by companies and training costs.
The British Chambers of Commerce argues that at 3.50 stg an hour, 15 percent of small firms are affected, while 4.25 stg would impact 55 percent.

Bass employs about 70,000 people, including 50,000 in its UK pubs most of them as bar staff. Earlier the company posted a 10 percent increase in its profits before tax to 318 million stg for the six months to April 12, 1997 driven by its managed pubs and 2,200 Holiday Inn empire.
